facts.statement: Budget 2025 extended to 31 March 2030: Section 10(4D) for IBU investment divisions, Section 10(4F) for non-resident aircraft/ship lease royalty and interest, Section 10(4H) capital-gains exemption on aircraft-leasing IFSC unit shares, Section 80LA for aircraft/ship leasing income, Section 9A fund-manager safe harbour, and Section 47(viiad) tax-neutral fund relocation.

IFSC withholding specifics: concessional 10% withholding on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; no deemed dividend for a listed foreign corporate entity in GIFT IFSC; interest on bonds listed on IFSC exchanges is taxable at 9% (plus surcharge and cess), and long-term bonds/RDBs listed on IFSC exchanges at 4%; thin capitalisation norms are relaxed for finance companies.

Transfer of specified securities by a non-resident or Category III AIF is not treated as a transfer for capital-gains purposes; 0% capital gains applies on specified securities in IFSC; dividend income is taxed in shareholder hands.

The Onshore Innovation to GIFT IFSC committee (chair G. Padmanabhan, ex-ED RBI; members included Nikhil Kamath, Lalit Keshre, Siddarth Pai and Nishith Desai) recommended: tax neutrality on relocation of offshore HoldCos to IFSC, a participation exemption for capital gains on share transfers by IFSC HoldCos, rationalisation of tax rates post-relocation, a dedicated LRS limit for IFSC investment separate from the general USD 250,000 limit, exclusion of Indian AIF/MF investments in GIFT IFSC entities from the RBI overseas-investment aggregate limit, simplified HoldCo incorporation, and a dedicated MCA official in GIFT IFSC.
facts.detail: Context: India is the 3rd largest startup ecosystem with 108+ unicorns and 99,000+ recognised startups; startup funding Jan 2014-May 2023 was about USD 141 billion (USD 66 billion in 2021-22); CEBR projects a USD 10 trillion economy by 2035.

facts.statement: The Authority itself is exempt from income-tax and all other taxes under Section 26 of the IFSCA Act, while IFSC units enjoy the 100% income-tax holiday for 10 consecutive years out of a 15-year window.
